facts.statement: The species Vastanavis cambayensis was described by Mayr and colleagues in 2010.
The genus Vastanavis was first described by Mayr and colleagues in 2007.
Fossils of Vastanavis date to the Early Eocene epoch.
Vastanavis lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Vastanavis belongs to the Neognathae group of birds.
The two known species of Vastanavis, V. eocaena and V. cambayensis, are found in the Cambay Formation.
facts.quote: It contains two species, Vastanavis eocaena and Vastanavis cambayensis; both are known from the Cambay Formation.

facts.statement: Vastanavis had at least semi-zygodactyl feet and was likely an arboreal bird.
facts.quote: Vastanavis was at least semi-zygodactyl, and most likely arboreal.

rejected.statement: Vastanavis was a parrot-like bird that lived in what is now western India during the Early Eocene.
rejected.quote: Vastanavis is a genus of parrot-like bird that lived in what is now western India in the Early Eocene.
